notes:
I found one place that qualifies. I couldn't confirm two others.

```json
{
  "picks": [
    {
      "name": "Canada Agriculture and Food Museum",
      "age_fit": "Youth (ages 3 to 17); Child (age 2 and under) free",
      "when": "Daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; free admission daily 4 p.m. to 5 p.m.",
      "price": "Youth (ages 3 to 17) $12.75 regular, taxes not included; age 2 and under free",
      "source_name": "Ingenium (Canada Agriculture and Food Museum)"
    }
  ]
}
```

- **What the museum's page says:** 
The hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. every day of the week.
 
Youth ages 3 to 17 pay $12.75 regular admission, and children 2 and under are free.
 
Admission is free daily between 4 p.m. and 5 p.m.

- **Summer kids' pass:** The page also lists a Canada Strong Pass. 
It gives free admission for kids 17 and under until September 7.
 I can't tell which year that refers to, so don't count on it for your dates.
- **Your dates:** The page I read is a summer 2026 snapshot. It doesn't show hours for August 30 to September 2 specifically.

**Not included**
- **Canadian Children's Museum:** Its own page lists hours 
for September 8 to December 9, 2026
, which starts after your window. The museum is also in Gatineau, across the river from Ottawa. I couldn't tie its hours to your dates.
- **Canadian Museum of Nature:** I only found its hours and ages on travel and review sites, not on the museum's own page. Reviewers also say 
younger children who learn best through hands-on play will find less to do.


I didn't find any zoos, aquariums or playgrounds on the operators' own pages.
